clue.text: Gets sex in centre wearing pair of smalls

indicators.note: a garment wraps around the wearer, so the pair of letters wraps around the middle word

parts.note: the first of two S's, S being short for small
the core is the centre of something

explanation.surface: Someone getting lucky in a city centre while wearing a couple of pairs of knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Smalls is British slang for underwear, but here a pair of smalls is just two S's for small, wrapped round the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is informal slang for succeeding in finding a sexual partner.

clue.text: Romantic couple not excited: back to being boring through trip

indicators.note: not means the word for excited is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
being up is being excited or worked up

indicators.note: something boring goes through a thing, so the last letter ends up inside the word for trip

parts.note: a ride is a trip

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word boring

explanation.surface: A dull romantic couple whose relationship has become a tedious journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic' looks like it describes the couple; it is the definition, capital R, for a poet of the Romantic movement. 'Excited' here means worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge, author of The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, is one of the major poets of the Romantic movement.

clue.text: One sacks Republican adviser on right

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the adviser comes before the right

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
an aide is an adviser or assistant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacks' looks like dismissal, but it means plunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider sacks, or pillages, the places attacked.

clue.text: Wife-swap and make love with Romeo — one goes both ways

to do is to make
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A racy scene of partner-swapping, with a hint that someone is bisexual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes both ways' sounds like a remark about sexuality; it describes a door hinged to open in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing door opens both inwards and outwards, so it moves both ways.

clue.text: Look around the empty place

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or behold
ca is short for circa, meaning around

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its insides, so only its outside letters stay

parts.note: the outer letters of the word the

explanation.surface: An instruction to search an empty building or spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to find it or put it in a particular place.

clue.text: Tree-hugger from left to disagree having ignored leader

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and ignoring it leaves it out

parts.note: to demur is to object or disagree

explanation.surface: An environmental activist breaks with the left wing over a disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree-hugger' suggests an eco-campaigner, but it is literal: a lemur clings to trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are tree-dwelling primates of Madagascar that cling to branches.

clue.text: See 8
One husband not in short swimming trunks

indicators.note: swimming means moving about in water, so these letters are jumbled
not in means the husband letter is left out of the pool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A husband is not wearing his skimpy swimming trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunks' looks like swimwear; it is the plural of torso. SHORT without H is rearranged, then I.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsi is a plural of torso, and a torso is the trunk of the body.

clue.text: Director from Italy collapsed first

indicators.note: first tells us the collapse word is placed ahead of the country letter

parts.note: a roof that collapsed fell in
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A film-maker from Italy fainted before anyone else did.
explanation.walkthrough: Federico Fellini, maker of La Dolce Vita, was indeed an Italian director, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was a celebrated Italian film director.

clue.text: Mad at flat décor ultimately concealed by Prime Minister: reason close allies lost respect?

indicators.note: mad suggests letters gone wild, so the words that follow are rearranged
the final letter of décor is hidden away, removing its last letter

parts.note: the word décor, which loses its last letter before joining the mix

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at the Prime Minister's lavish flat makeover, and the old friends who knew him best stopped respecting him.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the row over Boris Johnson's costly Downing Street flat refurbishment. 'ultimately concealed' drops the R of DÉCOR, leaving DECO; then AT FLAT DECO BY PRIME MINISTER is rearranged ('Mad') into the whole proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says knowing someone too well leads to disdain, which explains why intimate companions stop respecting each other.

clue.text: Tramp working to fill-in for top person

indicators.note: filling something in means occupying its inside, so the word for working goes in the middle

parts.note: to tramp is to march
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: The setter, Tramp, standing in for the boss at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Tramp is this puzzle's setter, so the clue reads as the setter deputising.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is the sovereign, the person at the very top of a state.

clue.text: Drunk intended to grab woman's bottom: big deal?

parts.note: high means intoxicated

indicators.note: grabbing takes hold of something, so the betrothed word closes round the letter

parts.note: one's intended is one's fiancé

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of woman

explanation.surface: A drunk fiancé groping a woman's backside, and someone asking whether it matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big deal?' sounds like a dismissive shrug; it is a large financial transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: High finance covers large-scale dealings of banks and corporations, where deals are huge.

clue.text: Growing business? Good — get firm, initially lost, to enter promotion

indicators.note: the good-plus-firm letters go into the word for promotion, entering it partway

parts.note: marketing is the business of promoting products

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for get firm is dropped

parts.note: to harden is to get firm

explanation.surface: A business plan pep talk: good news, the firm is moving into promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing business?' reads as a firm that is expanding, but the question mark points to a business that grows crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Market gardening is raising vegetables and fruit commercially for sale, a trade whose product literally grows.

clue.text: Woman did lie about duke

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for did lie goes round the title letter

parts.note: lay is the past tense of lie
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A woman told untruths about a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did lie' suggests telling lies; it is the past of lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is a polite term for a woman, and also the title held by a duke's wife or daughter.

clue.text: Firm with smoking gun? Fit with a silencer?

indicators.note: with joins the two parts side by side, the second after the first

parts.note: sound means solid and firm
a smoking gun is conclusive proof

explanation.surface: A company owning a just-fired gun, and whether to add a silencer.
explanation.walkthrough: The gun surface makes 'silencer' look like a firearm accessory; it is anything that stops noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To soundproof a room is to fit insulation that stops noise passing, so it acts as a silencer.

clue.text: Found holes in up-ended can: opened with sharp tool

indicators.note: in a down entry, up-ending turns a word upside down so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: a tin is a can
a lock is picked when opened with a pick

explanation.surface: Someone discovering punctures in an upturned can they prised open with a sharp tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found holes in' reads as literal punctures; it means picking holes in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find petty faults, the same idea as picking holes in something.

clue.text: Beats virus: a lot suffering

indicators.note: something suffering is damaged and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fighting off an infection while feeling very ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrival someone is to beat them in a contest.

clue.text: One might be scrambling with bride getting kit off

indicators.note: off can mean gone bad or wrong, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bride hurriedly undressing on her wedding night.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrambling is the British name for off-road motorcycle racing over rough ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirt bike is an off-road motorcycle used in scrambling competitions.

clue.text: Better talk after email is hacked

indicators.note: after places the word for talk behind the other part
hacked data is tampered with and scrambled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to orate is to give a formal talk

explanation.surface: A conversation goes better once someone's email account is broken into.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to make or become better, an improvement verb.

clue.text: Bowl over with star catching last from mid-wicket

indicators.note: catching holds something inside, so the star word closes round the letter

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: last from means take the final letter of the word given

parts.note: the final letter of mid-wicket

explanation.surface: A star cricketer bowling someone out with a catch at mid-wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-wicket is a fielding position in cricket; 'bowl over' is not a delivery but means astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to amaze them, as to stun them is.

clue.text: Race and Archie's skin linked with King Charles and Queen

indicators.note: the two pairs are intermixed, their letters interlinked in a new order

parts.note: the skin of Archie is its outside, its first and last letters
CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles's royal cipher
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A dig at a royal racism row over baby Archie's skin colour, involving King Charles and the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to a reported royal remark about the complexion of Prince Harry's son Archie. CR and ER are the royal ciphers, from the Latin Carolus Rex and Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at high speed, so it can stand for the verb race.

clue.text: Unknown state of steel that's wearing at front

indicators.note: at front places the wearing word before the other part

parts.note: someone in a coat is wearing it
steel means resolve or determination

explanation.surface: A puzzling condition of the metal that is being worn at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Indetermination is a state of being undetermined or not known with certainty.

clue.text: Supporter to wear yellow

parts.note: to don is to put on or wear
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A fan putting on the club's yellow colours.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic term for gold or yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money to a cause, so is one of its financial backers.

clue.text: Blows a fuse as resistance fades

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
something that ages grows old and fades

explanation.surface: An electrical circuit failing as its resistance drops.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical surface makes 'Blows a fuse' literal; it means loses one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who blows a fuse loses their temper, which is to say rages.

clue.text: Pulling through idle chat in middle of night, grabbing number

indicators.note: grabbing seizes and holds, so the chat word closes round the number letter

parts.note: yak is idle chatter
N is short for number
taken as written

indicators.note: middle of means the central letter of the word given

parts.note: the middle letter of night

explanation.surface: Pulling an all-nighter of gossip, grabbing a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Yanking is pulling sharply on something.

clue.text: Docking fee from price in the end after beer turns in barrel

indicators.note: after puts the price letter behind the rest
in places the turned word inside the container word

parts.note: a keg is a small barrel

indicators.note: turning around makes the word read backwards

parts.note: ale is a beer

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of price

explanation.surface: A charge for docking taken from the price of beer poured into a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docking fee' sounds like a penalty deducted from pay; it is a harbour charge for ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Keelage is a toll paid by a ship for anchoring or berthing in a harbour.

clue.text: See 8 Down
Arm-twisting? Getting robe over uniform

parts.note: to robe is to dress
uniform is U in the radio alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: Arm-twisting is figurative here: pressure or coercion.
